mechanism.gold: Requires Commerce licences for exports of advanced AI chips to countries of concern, with a 30-day congressional review and disapproval mechanism modelled on arms-sales review, and codifies the prohibition on the most capable chips for 18 months ; Commerce certification that exports of lesser chips do not divert US supply or foundry capacity or permit unauthorized remote access; an "American AI Victory Strategy." The AIPN conference letter also lists House Sec. 240 (AGI Preparedness Initiative), House Sec. 1502 (AI Incident and Vulnerability Reporting Program), and Senate Secs. 1634 (insider-threat reporting for large AI contractors), 1652–1655 (AI bill of materials, human oversight for use of force, biosecurity procurement for covered AI models, secure AI data centers) as provisions in play

mechanism.gold: Different design from SB 315: a liability shield — developer not liable for critical harms absent intent/recklessness if it publishes a safety & security protocol and transparency report; deemed compliant if bound by EU rules or a federal agency agreement; sunsets if federal law creates overlapping requirements
mechanism.got: Section 10: a developer shall not be held liable for critical harms if it did not intentionally or recklessly cause them and it published a safety and security protocol and a transparency report. Section 15: a developer must create a safety and security protocol documenting technical and organizational protocols to manage, assess, and mitigate risk of critical harm from its frontier models. Section 20: a developer must create a transparency report identifying the frontier model and summarizing assessment results and steps taken to address identified risks. Section 10(b): a developer is deemed compliant if it agrees to be bound by EU AI Act Article 56 safety requirements or enters an agreement with a federal agency for model access and evaluation. Section 10(c): a developer that enters a federal agency agreement shall file a certification with the Attorney General, and a materially false or misleading statement in it violates the Act. Section 25: a developer is deemed in compliance if it complies with another state's substantially similar frontier model safety and security framework. Section 25: the Act no longer applies if the federal government enacts a law or adopts regulations that establish overlapping requirements for developers of frontier models.

thresholds.gold: Frontier models defined by compute or cost
thresholds.got: Frontier model: trained using greater than 10^26 computational operations, such as integer or floating-point operations; or compute cost that exceeds $100,000,000.

mechanism.gold: Safety & security protocol; transparency reports every 90 days ; annual third-party audit (published within 90 days); whistleblower protections with private right of action (90-day window, clear-and-convincing standard) + anonymous channel with monthly updates; AG enforcement. Appears to be a clone of the original June 2025 RAISE Act text — same $5M/$100M compute-cost thresholds, same 100-death threshold, same audit/whistleblower structure that NY later stripped out. Effective dates are written as "Beginning January 1, 2026" — already past, since the bill hasn't moved
mechanism.got: Beginning on January 1, 2026, a large developer shall produce, implement, follow, and conspicuously publish a safety and security protocol. A large developer shall, not less than once every 90 days, produce and conspicuously publish a transparency report. A large developer shall record and retain for 5 years the specific tests used and results obtained in critical risk assessments. A large developer shall provide an internal process for anonymous employee disclosures, with a monthly update to the employee on the investigation. If a large developer violates section 7 or 9, the attorney general may bring a civil action for a civil fine and injunctive or declaratory relief. A large developer shall not discharge, threaten, or discriminate against an employee for reporting information that indicates the developer's activities pose a critical risk. Beginning on January 1, 2026, a large developer shall retain a reputable third-party auditor not less than once per year to produce a report on compliance, and must publish it not more than 90 days after completion. An employee alleging a whistleblower violation may bring a civil action not more than 90 days after the alleged violation, seeking injunctive relief, actual damages, and attorney fees.

thresholds.gold: Cost-based, not FLOP-based: "large developer" = trained a model costing ≥$5M in compute (at prevailing cloud prices) and ≥$100M aggregate compute cost in preceding 12 months;
thresholds.got: Large developer: developed a foundation model with computing power costing not less than $5,000,000.00 at prevailing cloud market prices; and within the preceding 12 months, foundation models with total computing power costing not less than $100,000,000.00. Foundation model: trained on a broad data set, designed for generality of output, and adaptable to a wide range of distinctive tasks.

penalties.got: Violation of section 7 or 9: civil fine of not more than $1,000,000.00 per violation, plus injunctive or declaratory relief, enforced by the attorney general; Whistleblower section violation: civil fine of not more than $500.00, deposited into the general fund; Employee civil action: employee may seek injunctive relief, actual damages, and reasonable attorney fees, witness fees, and court costs.
